title: Graph Beta: establish Foundation attempt input authority
description: Graph Beta prerequisite for task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038. Resolve, then land, the production authority source for the Foundation dispatch request’s launchTemplate and inputManifest instead of accepting an accidental caller copy. At planning time record the per-field decision “server-derived/durable” versus “caller-proposed but bounded and authenticated” for argv, cwd, environment, bootstrap credential digest, launch selection, limits, runtime observation, base identity, and workspace entries; unresolved fields block rather than default. Measurement at HEAD a42ae2f1f9168d13b8b786404fc47b366cc8edd9: FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_KEYS requires launchTemplate/inputManifest; packages/runner exports builders and workspace observers, but daemon production has no launch-template producer and its only durable inputManifest reader belongs to the separate sealed foundation-verification aggregate. This task creates the lawful production source/hydration seam. Stage: GRAPH BETA. Not in scope: attempt command registration, current-graph projection, claim/activation, provider dispatch internals, widening effect.activate, or editing the authoritative design.
definitionOfDone: Planning notes record a complete per-field authority matrix for launchTemplate and inputManifest, including why each field is server-derived/durable or caller-proposed; no field is left implicit, and any caller-proposed field has an exact authenticated payload allow-list and bound.

A focused production source/hydrator produces the exact FoundationAttemptLaunchTemplate and WorkspaceInputManifest for a project/session/node using approved durable facts and real runner/host observation surfaces; it never accepts caller-selected grant, runtime closure, slot, budget, lease, attempt, effect, or process-registration authority.

Workspace input is sealed through the production @moe/runner manifest builder against the observed base identity and actual bounded entries, while runtime/launch facts remain tied to server-owned provider capabilities; mismatched base, stale observation, missing workspace, hostile path/argv/environment, or unverifiable runtime fails closed with an exact stable code and layer.

Repeated reads of the same durable identity are byte-stable; conflicting durable/caller-proposed bytes refuse before claim, activation, launch, or process registration and leave zero durable/provider residue.

Focused tests exercise the production source with real durable store and filesystem/host seams, assert exact reason code and layer plus nonzero generated hostile-case counts, include one accepted control, and cover Windows path/argv behavior plus platform-neutral macOS/Linux rejection semantics without shell-normalizing authority.

Completion names task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038 as the production consumer and records the exact call-site/dependency edge; daemon typecheck/test and plain-Node provider construction execute with nonzero test evidence.

The `runtime` sub-object is NOT minted here: hand the three plain data fields to the runner's own observation and pinning surface so the runtime is freshly observed rather than asserted, exactly as `createClaudeRuntimePinRequest` is designed to require. Accept NO caller-selected grant, runtime closure, slot, budget, lease, attempt, effect or process-registration authority -- the contract comment at foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:91-96 already declares those authority-free by construction and this producer must not reintroduce any of them. Keep the file <=250 physical lines; split the per-field derivations into a sibling module rather than trimming a refusal branch.

Failing tests: (1) `baseIdentity` comes from the OBSERVED workspace base via the runner's scope/git observer, and a request proposing a different base is refused with an exact code and layer rather than honoured; (2) the caller may propose the PATH SET only -- for each proposed path the server observes `sha256` and `byteLength` itself and assigns `producer` from durable provenance, and a request supplying a digest that disagrees with the observed bytes is REFUSED, never preferred and never silently overwritten (assert the refusal, because silently correcting a hostile digest hides an attack); (3) a path absent from the workspace, a non-canonical path, a case-folding duplicate, a traversal escape, and an entry count over the runner's limit each refuse under the runner's OWN stable code surfaced with this module's layer -- do not restate the runner's rules locally; (4) one accepted control that seals a real small tree through `buildInputManifest` and asserts the exact returned manifest; (5) repeated hydration of the same durable identity is byte-stable. Assert the nonzero generated-case count, and assert zero residue on every refusal.

GREEN the hydrator. Create apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-input-manifest-hydrator.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge. It seals the workspace input through the PUBLIC `buildInputManifest` from bare `@moe/runner` against the observed base identity and the actually-observed bounded entries -- it must not reimplement path canonicalisation, case-folded duplicate detection, digest validation, producer normalisation or the entry limit, all of which `buildInputManifest` already owns (workspace/workspace-manifest.ts:62 and its PathSet at :29). This module's job is to OBSERVE the facts and hand them over, then surface the runner's failure code with this layer attached. Keep the file <=250 physical lines. Cross-platform: Windows path separators and case-insensitive filesystems interact with the runner's case-folding check, so the observation must produce canonical paths on Windows AND keep macOS/Linux rejection semantics intact -- never shell-normalise a path to make it acceptable, since normalising away a traversal is granting the authority the check exists to refuse.

Prove the ordering guarantee DoD 4 requires: conflicting durable versus caller-proposed bytes must refuse BEFORE claim, activation, launch or process registration, leaving zero durable and zero provider residue. Add tests that drive a conflicting request through both producers and assert (i) the refusal code and layer, (ii) that no work claim was taken, no activation was committed, no launch was attempted and no process registration exists -- assert each of those four absences explicitly against durable reads, not by inspecting the returned object, because a response-only assertion cannot tell a refusal that wrote from one that did not. Also assert byte-stability across two hydrations of the same durable identity by comparing canonical bytes, and assert the raw store event count is unchanged across every refusal path.

Mutation drills, one per authority claim, because a green suite cannot tell a server-derived field from a caller echo. Drill 1: make the template source prefer the caller's `argv` when present; a named step-2 test must go RED on its does-NOT-equal-the-proposed assertion -- if it stays green the test only checked the durable value and must be strengthened. Drill 2: make the hydrator accept the caller's `sha256` instead of the observed one; the step-4 hostile-digest test must go RED. Drill 3: make the base-identity mismatch branch fall through instead of refusing; that step-4 test must go RED. Drill 4: move the conflict check to AFTER the claim; the step-6 no-claim assertion must go RED, proving the ordering guarantee is real and not incidental. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion -- a drill that reddens by crashing, or on a different assertion, has not proven the binding. Restore exact bytes by re-editing (never `git checkout`, which is destructive in this shared worktree) and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted per drilled file. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE PER-FIELD AUTHORITY MATRIX REQUIRED BY DoD 1, decided here at planning time as a Graph Beta authority decision and NOT inferred from the existing caller-shaped FoundationAttemptDispatchRequest. Nine rows.

LAUNCH TEMPLATE.
1. argv -- SERVER-DERIVED. Argv is the command line of a real process; a caller-chosen argv is arbitrary code execution wearing a data field. Derived from the durable node mission plus server-owned provider capabilities. Caller may propose nothing.
2. bootstrapCredentialDigest -- SERVER-DERIVED. It digests a credential the daemon mints; accepting a caller digest lets the caller bind the launch to a credential it chose.
3. cwd -- SERVER-DERIVED from the workspace root durably bound to this attempt. A caller-proposed cwd is a traversal and blast-radius decision, not an input.
4. environment -- SERVER-DERIVED and allow-listed. Caller may propose nothing; a genuinely per-node variable must arrive from a durable node-spec field, never from the request.
5. launchSelection -- SERVER-DERIVED from server-owned provider capabilities. Currently typed `unknown`, which is itself a defect: an unbounded field cannot be authenticated, so this task gives it a bounded declared shape.
6. limits -- SERVER-DERIVED from durable policy and scheduler budget. Caller-proposed limits let a caller raise its own ceiling. Also currently `unknown`; same fix.
7. runtime.installedRoot / pinRoot / quotedObservation -- SERVER-DERIVED through real host observation. createClaudeRuntimePinRequest deliberately mints fs/facts/clock from three plain data fields so that no caller can hand pinning a runtime nobody observed; the quoted observation must come from the server-obtainable observation surface, never from the request.

INPUT MANIFEST.
8. baseIdentity -- SERVER-DERIVED from the OBSERVED workspace base via the runner's scope/git observer. The manifest is sealed against what was observed, never against what was asserted.
9. entries -- THE ONLY CALLER-PROPOSED ROW, and bounded: the caller may propose the PATH SET; the server observes sha256 and byteLength itself and assigns producer from durable provenance. A caller-supplied digest is refused on disagreement, never preferred and never silently corrected -- silently correcting a hostile digest hides the attack. The bound is the runner's own MAX_WORKSPACE_ENTRIES plus its canonical-path, case-folded-duplicate and producer rules.

No field is left implicit; the two `unknown` fields are closed rather than waved through. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) accepting the whole launchTemplate as caller-proposed-but-validated -- validation of an unbounded shape is not authentication, and rows 1-4 are execution authority; (b) minting the runtime observation in the daemon -- it would re-open exactly the seam the runner withholds observeInstalledClaudeRuntime to close; (c) one combined module -- the launch template and the workspace manifest have separate observation seams and separate refusal vocabularies and would exceed the per-file line target together; (d) re-validating a caller graphSnapshot here -- the durable current-graph answer belongs to task-dd4ffa0c and this task consumes it.

planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is a caller echo that reads as server authority: if a test asserts only that the produced value equals the durable one, code that prefers the caller when both are present still passes. Every matrix row therefore needs the does-NOT-equal-the-proposed assertion, and drill 1 exists to prove it. Second, silently correcting a hostile digest instead of refusing turns an attack into a no-op and destroys the evidence -- refuse, and assert the refusal. Third, ordering: a conflict detected AFTER the claim or activation leaves durable residue, so the four absences in step 6 must be asserted against durable reads rather than against the returned object; a response-only assertion cannot distinguish a refusal that wrote from one that did not. Fourth, do not restate the runner's workspace rules in the daemon -- a local reimplementation drifts and the tests would then police the copy rather than the production surface. Fifth, Windows: path separators and a case-insensitive filesystem interact with the runner's case-folding duplicate check, and shell-normalising a path to make it acceptable would grant exactly the authority the check refuses; keep macOS/Linux rejection semantics intact. Sixth, `launchSelection` and `limits` must not stay `unknown` -- an unbounded field cannot be authenticated, so leaving them would make DoD 1 unsatisfiable no matter what the notes claim. Seventh, close every SqliteEventStore handle and remove every temporary workspace on every path including refusals; a held handle kills the vitest worker and a leaked temp dir fails the next Windows case with EBUSY. Finally, this task's consumer (task-a9fd91c3) is BLOCKED, so DoD 6 is satisfied by naming the task id and the intended call site, not by claiming a live edge exists.
